Trzebinia Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Trzebinia, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are first recorded in Trzebinia in the 16th century, though significant community development began only after 1731; by 1921, 1,100 (22.9%) were mostly murdered at Auschwitz-Birkenau. This cemetery, established in 1815, holds an ohel over the graves of rabbis and tzadikim Mosze Jona Lewi (d. 1843), Izrael and Chaim Kluger (both d. 1869), and Awraham Lewi (d. 1895). Fenced with a funeral house by the interwar period, it received victims of the nearby Trzebionka forced-labor camp during WWII. The Jewish Committee in Trzebinia maintained the site through at least 1946, when a Holocaust mass-grave monument was erected; the Landsmanshaft of Trzebinia Jews led further cleanup in the 1980s-90s, and the ohel was rebuilt in 1990.
